# Subscription and native CLI accounts

Sub-contract of [Models](models.md); [INTEL-03](../capabilities.md#capability-register) owns
delivery status. The Provider configuration owner stays the only writer; official CLIs keep their
own credentials. No token import, copying, keychain read or second account database is allowed.

## Permitted routes (candidate 0166, OV-096)

Subscriptions run only where the vendor sanctions it: Fleet's own Sign in with ChatGPT registration
(multi-account, as OpenAI documents), the Codex app-server, and vendors' documented ACP modes,
including the official Copilot CLI and Grok Build executors added here. Claude subscription,
Antigravity and borrowed-client Copilot/Grok logins are retired with their data kept; see the
evidence table in [OV-096](../decisions.md). Multi-account below now applies to Codex only.

## Native CLI accounts (candidate 0163)

| Concern | Contract |
|---|---|
| Storage | `access.accounts` on the existing native-cli record: id, name, plan, `configDir`. The active account is mirrored in the existing access fields; `configDir: ""` means the CLI's own default home. Records written before 0163 read as one account. |
| Adding | Claude/Codex only (their official logins honour `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`CODEX_HOME`). The Host allocates `<app config>/native-cli-accounts/<cli>/<uuid>` (0700), runs the official login there and inspects that home. A duplicate identity is refused and its home discarded. Ten accounts at most. |
| Switching | Re-inspect the target home, then replace identity and catalog in one `mergeDiscoveredModels` transaction. The writer accepts a changed `configDir` only when the new access lists it among its saved accounts. |
| Continuation | The native continuation scope already hashes executor kind, home and account, so a switch starts a fresh native session and replays the Fleet transcript; another account's thread is never resumed. |
| Removal | Removing the current account first activates the next one. Only Fleet-allocated homes are deleted; the CLI default home never is. |
| Allowance | Each account is read through its own home; the adapter checks identity per read. Cache key: connection + account. |
| Auto-switch | Default off; needs two accounts. Leave an account only when an account-wide window reaches 98% (Claude model-scoped weeklies excluded); choose the saved account with the most headroom below 90%; never choose an unreadable account. Triggered by allowance reads and a five-minute Host sweep; five-minute cooldown per connection. A running turn finishes on its account; the next turn uses the new one. |

Why multi-account disappeared: candidate `25debe2f` hid the `fleet-openai-codex` OAuth template
(which carried accounts and auto-switch) in favour of native Codex, which then held one identity.
Grok and Copilot subscriptions kept their accounts throughout.

Comparison: Cockpit Tools (`源码参考/software/cockpit-tools`, v1.3.62) keeps an account index plus
detail files, refreshes quota on a scheduler, alerts with cooldown and auto-switches by
primary/secondary thresholds (`modules/codex_account_mutations_quota.rs`). Its ordinary switch
overwrites the CLI's `auth.json`/keyring, which Fleet does not do; its "instance" homes are the
adopted mechanism.

## Stability (candidate 0165)

Measured on 2026-10-06: `~/.codex/auth.json` was rewritten at 10:45 while Cockpit Tools was
running, and Fleet's first `account changed` failure followed at 10:45:36. Every outside switch of
an official CLI's own login (Cockpit Tools, a terminal `codex login`) made Fleet demand a
reconnect, because the connection is bound to that shared login. Cockpit is stable because it owns
its account store; nothing else rewrites it.

| Failure | Cause | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "Account changed, reconnect" | Saved identity vs a rewritten default login | A default-login connection follows the CLI: discovery, allowance reads, a five-minute sweep and the chat error adopt the new identity and catalog. If the new login is an account Fleet keeps in its own home, that home stays in use. Fleet homes cannot change from outside. A turn already admitted still fails its account fence and is retried after the sync. |
| "Revision conflict" on reconnect | Native writes were fenced on the global settings revision, so any unrelated write during a 5–7 s CLI check failed them | Fenced on this connection's own config only |
| "Sign in first" while signed in | Any ACP `authenticate` failure, and any message containing auth/login, meant signed out | Network causes are kept; only explicit refusals (`category=auth`, 401, "authentication required") mean signed out; Cursor's silent check says signed out *or* offline |
| Toast in the middle of the list | Feedback overlay lived inside the internally scrolling detail column | Anchored to the visible pane (browser test fails on the old layout) |

CodeBuddy's current failure is genuine (`session/new` → `Authentication required`, category auth).

## Interface

Each account is ZCode's original plan card (`PlanStatusCardSurface` with the shared allowance
section), peer to the model list rather than nested in a CLI card: email, plan and Current badges,
an in-use/standby/sign-in-needed status, **Use this account** on inactive cards, and a menu with
re-sign-in and confirmed removal. The heading carries **Add account**, mirroring Model list / Add
model; the existing auto-switch block follows. One account keeps the earlier single card. The
settings split panel is window-bounded and its two columns scroll independently.

Verification is measured, not judged from screenshots: `packages/ui/test/layoutAudit.ts` checks
overflow and untitled truncation, the `text-ui-*` scale, 24 px targets, accessible names, WCAG
contrast against the composited background and the radius hierarchy across zh/en, Zai light/dark
and 360/720 px; the account test also requires the same computed type per role as the single
account card and no text below `text-ui-sm` outside badges. The same audit runs against the live
review page over CDP. Finding outside this fix: the shared `text-foreground-subtle` token measures
3.93:1 in Zai Light, below 4.5:1; the audit holds that token to 3:1 until the design system
decides.

## CLI placement

Fleet keeps CLI executors inside Model settings beside subscriptions and API keys, because the
user chooses an account and model there. AionUi (separate Agents page for ACP CLIs), Paseo (ACP
provider catalogue in provider settings) and Orca (terminal agents plus a rate-limits view) show
both splits work. The deciding difference is harness ownership: a native executor runs its own
tools, permissions and session, so its card says **CLI** and its execution contract lives in
[Agent core](agent-core.md), not in this page. A separate Agents page is warranted only when
custom agent definitions (arbitrary commands, health checks) are added.
